title: CDS legs and par spread check

items.prompt: Under the lesson sign convention, both CDS legs are reported as positive present-value magnitudes. Which expression gives the protection buyer's signed net value?
items.explanation: The protection leg is an inflow and the premium leg is an outflow for the protection buyer, so signed net value is protection minus premium.

items.prompt: A CDS has a positive protection-leg present-value magnitude of USD 35 and a positive premium-leg present-value magnitude of USD 28. What is the protection buyer's signed net value in USD?
items.explanation: From the protection buyer's perspective, net value is 35 - 28 = +7.

items.prompt: In the lesson's exact default-time model, a one-year annual-pay CDS has scheduled-premium annuity 0.941764533584 model-years and exact accrued-on-default annuity 0.009608857782 model-years. Calculate the positive premium-leg present-value magnitude in USD for notional USD 1,000,000 and running spread 100 basis points (0.01 per year).
items.explanation: The exact total premium annuity is 0.941764533584 + 0.009608857782 = 0.951373391366 model-years. The positive premium magnitude is 0.01 × 1,000,000 × 0.951373391366 = USD 9,513.73391366.

items.prompt: A two-year quarterly CDS has notional USD 3,000,000 and running spread 125 basis points (0.0125 per year). Exact integration under the supplied constant-hazard model gives scheduled-premium annuity 1.829782217887 model-years and accrued-on-default annuity 0.011512762522 model-years. Calculate the positive premium-leg magnitude in USD.
items.explanation: The total exact premium annuity is 1.841294980409 model-years. Multiplying 0.0125 × 3,000,000 × 1.841294980409 gives USD 69,048.56176534. The accrued factor comes from integrating default time, not a half-period replacement.

items.prompt: For a one-year CDS, exact integration over modeled default time gives a discounted risk-neutral default-density integral of 0.019411822139. Calculate the positive protection-leg magnitude in USD for notional USD 1,000,000 and recovery rate 0.40.
items.explanation: Loss given default is 1 - 0.40 = 0.60. The exact protection magnitude is 1,000,000 × 0.60 × 0.019411822139 = USD 11,647.0932834.

items.prompt: Use the exact flat-hazard protection formula N(1-R)λ[1-exp(-(r+λ)T)]/(r+λ). Calculate the positive protection-leg magnitude in USD for N = USD 3,000,000, R = 0.35, λ = 0.05 per year, r = 0.03 per year, and T = 2 years.
items.explanation: Here r + λ = 0.08. Substitution gives 3,000,000 × 0.65 × 0.05 × [1 - exp(-0.16)] / 0.08 = USD 180,199.757197. This discounts over actual modeled default time through the integral's closed form.

items.prompt: Calculate the zero-upfront par spread in basis points per year when the exact premium annuity is 0.951373391366 model-years and the exact protection factor is 0.011647093283 per unit notional.
items.explanation: The par annual decimal spread is 0.011647093283 / 0.951373391366 = 0.0122423996602. Multiplying by 10,000 gives 122.423996602 basis points per year; notional cancels.

items.prompt: A different exact default-time model produces scheduled-premium annuity 1.829782217887 model-years, accrued-on-default annuity 0.011512762522 model-years, and protection factor 0.060066585732 per unit notional. Calculate its zero-upfront par spread in basis points per year.
items.explanation: The exact total premium annuity is 1.841294980409. The par spread is 0.060066585732 / 1.841294980409 = 0.0326219244453 per year, or 326.219244453 basis points per year.
